description: Journey — once the user's game is understood (any game: no character, enemy, level, ending or known genre is required). Record what the game contains; for a known genre, its definition of done and the common frame (title / pause / end screens, sound, HUD, touch controls, a way to win or lose when the game has an end) are proposals to offer, recorded when the user takes them. Content is data, not code: generic systems in code (kits, parameters, hooks); levels, characters, weapons, items, balance, texts, assets and inputs as data read at run time; clips, bones, grips and sizes from each asset's passport, never written in code. Persist a versioned Game Completion Contract with revision checking. Read get_completion_report for its schema and a proposed contract. Required, optional and excluded capabilities describe the actual intended experience. 0 credits.

contract.description: GameCompletionContract matching the versioned schema returned by get_completion_report.

expected_revision.description: Current revision of the PROJECT (the `revision` field get_completion_report returns, also for a project with no contract yet; it is not a contract counter and 0 is never right). The save is refused with revision_conflict (actual revision in details) if the project changed since.

project_id.description: Game Kit project id (gkp_…). Not a dedicated-server project (gpj_…) nor a Library item.

workspace_id.description: Workspace authorized by the current key. Never infer another user’s workspace.
